topic: Venus Protocol (health factor / liquidation protection) and PancakeSwap (v3 + Infinity LP rebalancing) on BNB Smart Chain (chain 56) — interfaces, addresses, and math for AiKi
executive_summary:
Verified from primary sources: Venus's on-chain risk metric is NOT a health factor. Core Pool `Comptroller.getAccountLiquidity(address)` returns `(uint256 error, uint256 liquidity, uint256 shortfall)` — two USD-denominated 1e18 mantissas, not a ratio. A position is liquidatable iff `shortfall > 0`. Isolated Pools split the metric in two: `getAccountLiquidity` uses the **liquidation threshold**, `getBorrowingPower` uses the **collateral factor**; in the Core Pool CF == LT, so the two collapse. Any "health factor" AiKi displays must be synthesized off-chain from per-market prices, balances and LT — Venus gives you no HF getter. Build the HF as Σ(collateral·price·LT) / Σ(borrow·price) and cross-check that it crosses 1.0 exactly when `shortfall` goes positive.

The custody question resolves favorably: `repayBorrowBehalf(address borrower, uint256 repayAmount)` is confirmed in Venus's own `VTokenInterfaces.sol` on `VBep20Interface`. A third party can repay any borrower's debt with only its **own** underlying-token approval to the vToken — no approval, delegation, or custody from the borrower. So an AiKi agent can defend a Venus position with a treasury of stables and zero access to user collateral. That is the single most important architectural fact in this report.

PancakeSwap v3 remains live on BSC; `NonfungiblePositionManager` = `0x46A15B0b27311cedF172AB29E4f4766fbE7F4364` (confirmed on BscScan as "Pancake V3 Positions NFT-V1 (PCS-V3-POS)", deployed block 26931961). PancakeSwap Infinity (formerly v4) shipped on BNB Chain in April 2025 with CLAMM + LBAMM pool types, hooks, and a singleton Vault with flash accounting — v3 continues to operate alongside it.

Not verified this run and left as gaps: Venus ResilientOracle address/heartbeat/deviation, published numeric close factor and liquidation incentive, PancakeV3Factory address, Infinity's position-manager addresses, live subgraph endpoints, and whether Gamma/Steer/ICHI/Bunni run on BSC. Do not ship against any of those from memory.

findings.claim: Venus has no on-chain health factor. The Core Pool Comptroller exposes USD liquidity/shortfall, and liquidation is triggered by shortfall > 0, not by a ratio crossing 1.
findings.detail:
Verified signature (Isolated Pools Comptroller reference, identical shape in Core Pool):

`function getAccountLiquidity(address account) external view returns (uint256 error, uint256 liquidity, uint256 shortfall)`

Both `liquidity` and `shortfall` are USD values scaled 1e18 (mantissa), and at most one is non-zero. Venus's liquidation doc states the underlying calculation as `(Collateral Value × Collateral Factor) / Borrow Value` — i.e. the ratio form. Venus's docs call the metric "account liquidity"; "health factor" appears only in the user-facing leveraged-positions guide, not as a contract getter.

Derived HF for AiKi (equivalent, and crosses 1.0 exactly when shortfall becomes positive):

HF = Σ_i (vTokenBalance_i × exchangeRate_i × price_i × LT_i) / Σ_j (borrowBalance_j × price_j)

All factors are 1e18 mantissas. Note this differs from Aave: Aave returns `healthFactor` directly from `getUserAccountData`; Venus does not, and Venus's Core Pool collapses collateral factor and liquidation threshold into one value.

findings.claim: Isolated Pools split the metric: getAccountLiquidity uses the liquidation threshold, getBorrowingPower uses the collateral factor. Using the wrong one mis-prices the liquidation boundary.
findings.detail:
Verbatim from the Isolated Pools Comptroller reference:

`function getAccountLiquidity(address account) external view returns (uint256 error, uint256 liquidity, uint256 shortfall)`
`function getBorrowingPower(address account) external view returns (uint256 error, uint256 liquidity, uint256 shortfall)`
`function getHypotheticalAccountLiquidity(address account, address vTokenModify, uint256 redeemTokens, uint256 borrowAmount) external view returns (uint256 error, uint256 liquidity, uint256 shortfall)`

Doc language: a user may borrow based on the collateral factor, but if borrowing "exceeds an amount calculated using the market's corresponding liquidation threshold, the borrow is eligible for liquidation." So in Isolated Pools LT ≥ CF and there is a buffer band between "cannot borrow more" and "can be liquidated". In the Core Pool, CF = LT and that band is zero.

For AiKi: liquidation-risk monitoring must read `getAccountLiquidity`. `getBorrowingPower` answers a different question (headroom to open new debt) and will report danger too early. `getHypotheticalAccountLiquidity` is the correct pre-flight simulator for "what does this repay/withdraw do to the position" — use it to size a defensive repay before broadcasting.

findings.claim: A third party CAN repay a Venus borrower's debt with no custody of, and no approval from, the borrower. This makes non-custodial agent-side liquidation protection possible.
findings.detail:
Confirmed verbatim in Venus's own source (`VBep20Interface`):

`function repayBorrow(uint repayAmount) external returns (uint);`
`function repayBorrowBehalf(address borrower, uint repayAmount) external returns (uint);`
`function liquidateBorrow(address borrower, uint repayAmount, VTokenInterface vTokenCollateral) external returns (uint);`
`function mintBehalf(address receiver, uint mintAmount) external returns (uint);`

Approval direction: `repayBorrowBehalf` pulls underlying from `msg.sender` (the payer), so the **agent** must `approve(vToken, amount)` on the underlying BEP-20. The borrower approves nothing and signs nothing. `repayAmount = type(uint256).max` is the Compound-v2 convention for full repay (unverified for Venus specifically — see gaps).

Architectural consequence for AiKi: an agent holding a stablecoin float can top up any monitored Venus position permissionlessly. It cannot withdraw collateral, cannot rebalance, and cannot be drained by a compromised user key. The trust surface is only "agent spends its own money on the right borrower." `mintBehalf` similarly lets an agent add collateral to a user's supply position without custody — but note `mintBehalf` credits vTokens to `receiver`, so verify whether the receiver has that market entered before relying on it to raise HF.

findings.detail:
Verbatim from `deployments/bscmainnet_addresses.json` on the `develop` branch:

findings.claim: Venus Core Pool vs Isolated Pools is a hard architectural split, not a tier label — separate Comptroller instances, separate risk parameters, separate liquidation semantics.
findings.detail:
Core Pool: one Comptroller (the Unitroller at `0xfD36E2c2a6789Db23113685031d7F16329158384`), all markets cross-collateralized, collateral factor equals liquidation threshold.

Isolated Pools: each pool is its own Comptroller instance with its own market set, deployed and tracked through a PoolRegistry. Collateral factor and liquidation threshold are distinct per market, so `getBorrowingPower` and `getAccountLiquidity` diverge.

For AiKi this means position discovery is per-Comptroller: there is no single global "list a user's Venus positions" call. You must enumerate pools from PoolRegistry, then `getAssetsIn(account)` per Comptroller, then `getAccountSnapshot(account)` per vToken. Budget for N+M RPC round-trips per user per poll, or use multicall3. The Core Pool alone is a reasonable v1 scope — it holds the large majority of Venus TVL — with Isolated Pools as a later expansion.

findings.claim: Venus liquidation parameters: close factor and liquidation incentive are per-market governance values, not protocol constants. Only illustrative numbers (50% close factor, 110% incentive) appear in the docs.
findings.detail:
The liquidation guide shows a worked example using a 50% close factor and a 110% liquidation incentive (10% bonus to the liquidator), but explicitly does not state these as protocol-wide defaults. Both are stored as mantissas on the Comptroller (`closeFactorMantissa`, `liquidationIncentiveMantissa` in the Compound-v2 lineage) and are set by Venus governance per market.

Max seizable in one liquidation call:
  maxRepay = borrowBalance × closeFactorMantissa / 1e18
  seizeTokens = (repayAmount × price_borrowed × liquidationIncentiveMantissa) / (price_collateral × exchangeRate_collateral)

Do NOT hardcode 0.5 / 1.1. Read the mantissas from the target Comptroller at runtime and cache with a short TTL plus a governance-event invalidation. These values changing under you is a realistic failure mode for a bot that sizes repays.

findings.claim: PancakeSwap v3 NonfungiblePositionManager on BSC mainnet is 0x46A15B0b27311cedF172AB29E4f4766fbE7F4364, live and holding ~4.7M minted positions.
findings.detail:
DEPLOYED. Confirmed via BscScan token tracker and Blockscan: the contract is labeled "PancakeSwap V3: Nonfungible Position Manager", token name "Pancake V3 Positions NFT-V1" (symbol PCS-V3-POS), BEP-721, first deployed at BSC block 26931961, total supply reported ~4,744,873 positions.

The same address is used on several other chains (Arbitrum, Polygon zkEVM appear in the same search) because PancakeSwap deploys v3 deterministically — do not treat address equality across chains as a bug.

PancakeSwap v3 is a Uniswap v3 fork, so the NPM ABI is the Uniswap v3 `INonfungiblePositionManager` shape (mint/increaseLiquidity/decreaseLiquidity/collect/positions). The struct field names given in the interfaces section follow the Uniswap v3 periphery spec; I did not fetch PancakeSwap's own copy of the interface this run, so treat exact struct member ordering as needing a one-time ABI verification against BscScan before you encode calldata.

NOTE: PancakeV3Factory, SwapRouter, QuoterV2, TickLens and MasterChefV3 addresses were NOT obtained — docs pages 403'd/404'd. See gaps.

findings.claim: PancakeSwap Infinity (formerly v4) DID ship, launching on BNB Chain in April 2025, introducing hooks, multiple AMM types (CLAMM and LBAMM), custom fees, and flash accounting. v3 continues to run.
findings.detail:
MARKETING/blog-tier, corroborated across PancakeSwap's own blog and third-party coverage: Infinity launched on BNB Chain first (BanklessTimes dates it 2025-04-28), with Ethereum in the same initial round and other chains planned.

What changed vs v3:
- Multiple pool types under one system: CLAMM (concentrated liquidity, v3-like) and LBAMM (liquidity book, bin-based, Trader-Joe-like).
- Hooks: externally deployed contracts registered to a pool that execute custom logic at swap/liquidity lifecycle points. Templates at github.com/pancakeswap/pancake-v4-hooks-template.
- Custom fee structures per pool.
- Flash accounting via a singleton vault (net-settlement instead of per-hop token transfers).

For AiKi's rebalancing category this is a strategic fork in the road: Infinity hooks could let a rebalancing policy live *inside* the pool rather than as an external keeper, but v3 is where the liquidity and the tooling maturity are today. Ship the v3 NPM keeper path first; treat Infinity as a second-phase surface. I could NOT verify Infinity's deployed BSC addresses, its position-manager interface, or current TVL split vs v3 — the developer docs 403'd. Do not write Infinity integration code from this finding alone.

findings.claim: The v3 fee-accrual, time-in-range, and impermanent-loss math for a PancakeSwap v3 position (v3 fork of Uniswap v3).
findings.detail:
MEMORY-SOURCED (Uniswap v3 whitepaper §6.3 / periphery), not fetched this run — verify before shipping.

Fees owed on a position (tickLower=l, tickUpper=u, liquidity=L):
  f_inside = f_global − f_below(l) − f_above(u)
  where f_below(l) = f_outside(l) if tick ≥ l else f_global − f_outside(l)
        f_above(u) = f_global − f_outside(u) if tick ≥ u else f_outside(u)
  owed = L × (f_inside_now − feeGrowthInsideLast) / 2^128
  Computed per token0/token1, with Q128.128 fixed point and deliberate uint256 underflow wrapping.
Cheapest correct path: `NonfungiblePositionManager.collect` with `amount0Max/amount1Max = type(uint128).max` in a static call — it returns exactly the collectable amounts without needing tick-bitmap math.

Time-in-range: integrate an indicator over blocks/time, TIR = Σ Δt·1[l ≤ tick_t < u] / Σ Δt. Sourced either from Swap events (exact) or periodic `slot0()` sampling (approximate; biased by sampling interval — use event-driven for anything you charge for).

Impermanent loss vs HODL for a v3 range, with p = price ratio P1/P0, and range [pa, pb]:
  Position value at P is the standard v3 amounts formula; IL = V_position(P) / V_hodl(P) − 1. For the full-range case this reduces to the v2 result IL = 2√p/(1+p) − 1. Concentrating amplifies IL by roughly 1/(1 − (pa/pb)^(1/4)) near the range center — treat that as intuition, not a shipped constant.

gaps: Venus ResilientOracle: address on BSC, which underlying feeds it aggregates (Chainlink / Binance oracle / TWAP / pivot+bound design), heartbeat, and deviation threshold — NOT FETCHED. This directly bounds agent reaction latency and is the single biggest missing input for AiKi's health-factor SLA. Get it from https://github.com/VenusProtocol/oracle deployments and the Chainlink BSC feed pages (each feed has its own heartbeat/deviation, typically differing per asset).

Venus published numeric close factor and liquidation incentive: the liquidation doc shows 50% and 110% only as illustrative example values and explicitly does not state protocol defaults. Read closeFactorMantissa and liquidationIncentiveMantissa live from the target Comptroller; do not hardcode.

Whether Venus accepts `repayAmount = type(uint256).max` as the full-repay sentinel in repayBorrowBehalf — Compound-v2 convention, unverified for Venus.

Venus subgraph / REST API for positions: NOT INVESTIGATED. Verify endpoints answer before designing an indexer dependency; have an RPC+multicall3 fallback path regardless.

Pull the ABI from the verified BscScan contract before encoding calldata. Known fork divergence risk: PancakeSwap adds MasterChefV3 farming, and staked positions are held by MasterChefV3, not the user — a rebalancer must handle the staked case (withdraw/harvest via MasterChefV3) separately.

PancakeSwap Infinity deployed addresses on BSC (Vault, CLPoolManager, BinPoolManager, position managers), the hook permission-flags encoding, and whether Infinity has its own NPM-equivalent — developer docs 403'd. Also unverified: current TVL/volume split between v3 and Infinity on BSC, which determines whether a v3-only rebalancer is still the right first target.

v3 fee-growth, time-in-range and impermanent-loss formulas given in findings are MEMORY-SOURCED from the Uniswap v3 whitepaper (§6.3) and periphery, not fetched this run. The feeGrowthInside math relies on deliberate uint256 underflow wrapping — verify against the actual Pool source. Prefer the empirical path: eth_call `collect` with amountMax = type(uint128).max to read collectable fees exactly.

Subgraph endpoints for PancakeSwap pools/positions/ticks and whether they answer in 2026: NOT INVESTIGATED. The Graph hosted service was sunset (2024) and PancakeSwap subgraphs moved to The Graph decentralized network / self-hosted endpoints requiring an API key. Assume an API key and a paid query budget are required; verify a live query before designing around it. One lead seen but not fetched: SubQuery publishes a BSC PancakeSwap v3 indexer quickstart (https://subquery.network/doc/indexer/quickstart/quickstart_chains/bsc-pancakeswap-v3.html) as an alternative indexing path.

Existing automated rebalancing vaults on BSC (Gamma, Steer, ICHI, Bunni): NOT INVESTIGATED AT ALL — zero evidence gathered either way. Do not assume presence or absence. This is a required competitive-benchmark task before scoping AiKi's rebalancing category.
aiki_implications: Non-custodial liquidation protection is BUILDABLE on Venus today, and this is the strongest product wedge found. `repayBorrowBehalf(address borrower, uint256 repayAmount)` requires only the agent's own approval to the vToken. AiKi can run a protection agent that holds a stablecoin float and tops up user positions without ever touching user collateral, without a delegation registry, and without the user signing anything at defense time. Trust surface reduces to 'agent spends its own money correctly' — which is exactly the kind of claim AiKi's trust layer is meant to attest.

Do NOT model Venus as Aave. There is no `healthFactor` getter. Build HF in AiKi's own indexer as Σ(collateral·price·LT)/Σ(borrow·price), and assert in tests that HF crossing 1.0 coincides with `getAccountLiquidity().shortfall` going positive. Use `getAccountLiquidity` (liquidation threshold), never `getBorrowingPower` (collateral factor), for danger detection — the latter alarms early and will burn agent capital on unnecessary repays.

Interest accrual is a correctness trap. `borrowBalanceStored` is a view but stale; `borrowBalanceCurrent` is non-view and must be read via eth_call. A monitor built on the stored variant systematically UNDER-estimates debt and will defend too late. Use `getAccountSnapshot` per market for the batch read, and reconcile against `borrowBalanceCurrent` before sizing an actual repay.

Agent reaction latency is oracle-bounded, and that bound is currently unknown. Until the ResilientOracle heartbeat and deviation threshold are pinned down, AiKi cannot state a defensible protection SLA. In a fast move the oracle updates, the position becomes liquidatable, and third-party liquidators race the protection agent in the same block. Design for that: the agent competes on latency and gas, not on privilege. Treat 'protection failed because a liquidator won the block' as an expected outcome to be priced and disclosed, not an exception.

Use `getHypotheticalAccountLiquidity` as a mandatory pre-flight before every defensive action. It lets the agent compute the minimum repay that restores a target HF buffer, rather than over-repaying. That directly controls the agent's capital efficiency and is the difference between a viable float and an unbounded one.

Position discovery on Venus is N+M RPC calls per user (enumerate markets, then snapshot each) with no global getter, and Isolated Pools multiply this by the number of pools. Batch through multicall3 and scope v1 to the Core Pool via the Unitroller at 0xfD36E2c2a6789Db23113685031d7F16329158384. Do not make the indexer a hard dependency — no Venus subgraph or REST endpoint was verified live in 2026, so the RPC path must be the primary, not the fallback.

Ship LP rebalancing against PancakeSwap v3 (NPM 0x46A15B0b27311cedF172AB29E4f4766fbE7F4364), not Infinity. Infinity is real and live on BNB Chain since April 2025, but its deployed addresses and interfaces could not be verified and its hook model would restructure the whole design. v3 has ~4.7M minted positions and a known Uniswap-v3-shaped ABI. Revisit Infinity hooks as a phase-2 differentiator once the v3 keeper is earning.

PancakeSwap v3 rebalancing is NOT custody-free the way Venus repay is. decreaseLiquidity/collect/mint on the NPM require the caller to be the position owner or an approved operator, so AiKi must hold an ERC-721 approval — a materially larger trust grant than the Venus path. Scope this explicitly: per-token `approve` beats `setApprovalForAll`, and the difference should be surfaced to users and attested. Additionally, MasterChefV3-staked positions are owned by MasterChefV3, not the user, so the rebalancer needs a distinct unstake/restake path.

Two categories, two trust tiers — make that the product story. Health-factor defense needs zero user authority and can be offered near-universally; LP rebalancing needs NFT operator authority and should carry stronger attestation, tighter scoping, and revocation UX. Conflating them in one permission prompt would waste the main advantage of the Venus path.

Before committing engineering to the rebalancing category, close the competitive gap: whether Gamma, Steer, ICHI or Bunni operate on BSC was not investigated at all. If mature managed-range vaults already run there, AiKi's differentiator must be the agent/trust layer rather than the rebalancing math itself. That is a scoping decision, and it is currently uninformed.
